title: Cascade-Correlation Growth Walkthrough
summary: Step through candidate training, installation, and freezing on a tiny constructive network.
learning_goals: Distinguish output-weight training from candidate-unit training.
See why the selected hidden unit is frozen after installation.
Connect residual correlation to incremental network growth.

title: Residual Correlation Playground
summary: Move a candidate unit's weights and see how its activation pattern correlates with residual error on a toy XOR problem.
learning_goals: Understand why Cascade-Correlation trains candidate units against residual error.
See why absolute correlation magnitude matters more than sign.
Connect a candidate hidden unit's activation pattern to a growth decision.

title: Constructive Algorithm Taxonomy
summary: Explore constructive-algorithm processes: when to modify structure, what to modify, and how to choose new parameters.
learning_goals: Separate construction, pruning, and merging as structural operations.
Distinguish global and local performance signals as growth triggers.
Understand STDC as construction whose control or parameters depend on spike times.

title: Simulation Expansion and Contraction
summary: Move low- or high-disruption components between surrounding and simulated sets to see why thesis-derived constructive spiking algorithms treat growth as careful simulation expansion.
learning_goals: Distinguish construction/pruning in memory from expansion/contraction of the simulated set.
Explain why low-disruption additions are more biologically plausible in spiking simulations.
Connect simulation expansion to later STDP-based parameter calculation for constructed synapses.

title: Evolving Spiking Lineage Cards
summary: Read a source-linked, not-human-reviewed synthesis of base eSNN candidate calculation and novelty/merge decisions, then use cautious paper cards to separate supervised adaptive-structure and unsupervised structural-plasticity branches without overclaiming later mechanism details.
learning_goals: Trace the base eSNN order from current-input spike ranks to candidate parameters and then a same-class novelty/merge decision.
Separate supervised class-labelled eSNN/adaptive-structure work from Roy2017's unsupervised structural-plasticity branch.
Separate reviewed eSNN lineage context from pending exact growth-rule details.
Connect Schliebs2013, Wysoski2010, Kasabov2013, Wang2014, and the shared Roy2017 bridge to the thesis taxonomy without duplicating paper records.
Use bundle readiness notes to decide which claims are safe for public teaching artifacts.
Reject source-boundary claims that turn metadata, titles, or thesis vocabulary into verified method mechanics.

title: What Counts as Evidence for More Capacity?
summary: Probe the distinct capacity-growth signals in Dynamic Node Creation, Cascade-Correlation, and Platt's Resource-Allocating Network without collapsing their training or stabilization rules.
learning_goals: Distinguish a global training plateau from candidate usefulness and local novelty.
Explain why Cascade-Correlation's correlation score selects a feature rather than acting alone as the need-for-growth signal.
Compare continued backpropagation, frozen installed features, and local allocation followed by LMS/center adaptation.

title: GNG, GWR, and Hidden-Feature Growth
summary: Separate periodic error-driven GNG insertion, activity-and-habituation-gated GWR insertion, and supervised hidden-feature growth.
learning_goals: Distinguish periodic accumulated-error growth in GNG from immediate two-threshold growth in GWR.
Separate input-space prototype and topology growth from supervised hidden-feature growth.
Connect each comparison claim to a runnable trace or source-boundary note.

title: Where Do the New Parameters Live?
summary: Compare bottleneck adapters, LoRA, and Mixture of LoRA Experts by where each puts its new parameters, what removing them costs, and what stays frozen.
learning_goals: Distinguish adding new layers inside a block from adding a low-rank delta to a matrix that already exists.
State what removal costs in each case, and why a merged LoRA is subtracted rather than deleted.
Explain why MoLE adds no capacity at all: the experts are already trained, and only the gate is learned.

title: Depth and Width from Existing Weights
summary: Compare Net2Net's function-preserving expansion, G_stack's re-trained depthwise stacking, and progressive networks' frozen columns with lateral reuse — including a live function-preservation check.
learning_goals: Distinguish expansion that preserves the function at the instant of growth from expansion that only carries the weights forward as an initialization.
Explain why Net2WiderNet divides outgoing weights by the replication count, and why it then adds noise anyway.
State what progressive networks buy by freezing every earlier column, and what they pay for it.

title: Capacity You Can Write, Directions You Can Read
summary: Follow product-key memory from billion-parameter capacity through 128B scaling and sparse slot updates, then contrast it with an SAE read-out that diagnoses and steers an existing model without enlarging that model.
learning_goals: Explain how sparse lookup makes a very large learned value table usable without activating all of its capacity.
Distinguish adding writable model parameters from fitting an auxiliary read-out over activations that already exist.
State sparse memory finetuning's low-interference result as this paper's measured claim, not as a guarantee of sparse updates.
